Root Base Class for Normal-Block Models

Source: R/NormalBlockBase.R
NormalBlockBase.Rd

R6 abstract class shared by the variance-block (NormalBlockVarBase) and mean-block (NormalBlockMeanBase) model families.

Public fields

data

object of NormalBlockData class, with responses and design matrix

Active bindings

inference_method

inference procedure used (heuristic or integrated with EM)

n

number of samples

p

number of responses per sample

d

number of variables (dimensions in X)

d0

number of zero-inflation covariates (dimensions in X0)

who_am_I

a description of the model

q

number of blocks

n_edges

number of edges of the network (non null coefficient of the sparse precision matrix Omega)

objective

evolution of the objective function during (V)EM algorithm

loglik

(or its variational lower bound)

deviance

(or its variational lower bound)

entropy

entropy of the (variational) posterior distribution of the clustering, -sum(tau * log(tau)): 0 when the clustering is known. Only the discrete partition is completed, as in the ICL of Biernacki, Celeux and Govaert (2000); the latent vectors W of the variance-block family are integrated out, not completed.

penalty_terms

data frame with one row per group of parameters: its name (group), its number of free parameters (nu) and the number of independent observations informing it (N), so that the group costs nu * log(N) in the BIC. As in the ICL of Daudin, Picard and Robin (2008) for SBMs and Keribin et al. (2015) for latent block models, the cluster proportions are charged log(p) (the variables are the units being clustered), parameters shared by every cell of a block log(n * p), and the remaining ones log(n).

nb_param

number of free parameters in the model, sum(penalty_terms$nu)

penalty

BIC penalty, sum(nu * log(N)) over penalty_terms

BIC

Bayesian information criterion, deviance + penalty (lower is better); built on the ELBO when the clustering is unknown and the likelihood is not available in closed form.

ICL

integrated completed likelihood criterion, BIC + 2 * entropy (lower is better); equal to the BIC when the clustering is known.

EBIC

extended BIC of Foygel and Drton (2010) with gamma = 1/2, BIC + 2 * n_edges * log(dim), where dim is the dimension of the network: q for the variance-block family (network between clusters), p for the mean-block family (network between variables).

criteria

a vector with loglik, BIC and number of parameters

sparsity

(overall sparsity parameter)

sparsity_term

(sparsity_term term in log-likelihood due to sparsity)

memberships

the p x q matrix of cluster memberships: indicators for a known clustering, posterior probabilities (tau) otherwise

clustering

the cluster label of each variable (MAP for an unknown clustering), named after the columns of Y

cluster_sizes

given as a vector of cluster sizes

elements_per_cluster

given as the list of elements contained in each cluster

NormalBlockBase$new()

Create a new NormalBlockBase object.

Usage

NormalBlockBase$new(data, q, sparsity = 0, control, zero_inflation = FALSE)

Arguments

data

object of NormalBlockData class, with responses and design matrix

q

number of block/cluster

sparsity

sparsity penalty on the network density

control

structured list of more specific parameters, to generate with NB_control

zero_inflation

whether the concrete subclass models zero-inflation; set by the ZI subclasses themselves, not meant to be set by the end user. When FALSE, the (costly) zero-inflation probability fit (kappa/B0) is skipped entirely, since it would otherwise never be used downstream.

Returns

A new NormalBlockBase object

NormalBlockBase$update()

Update the parameters of a model in place. Each argument applies to the families or variants named in parentheses; NA (the default) leaves the parameter unchanged.

Usage

NormalBlockBase$update(
  B = NA,
  dm1 = NA,
  C = NA,
  Omega = NA,
  gamma = NA,
  mu = NA,
  alpha = NA,
  M = NA,
  S = NA,
  ll_list = NA,
  warm_started = NA,
  clustering_init = NA
)

Arguments

B

regression coefficients (all models)

dm1

inverse noise variances of the variables (variance-block)

C

cluster memberships: indicators, or posterior probabilities (all models)

Omega

precision matrix: between clusters (variance-block) or between variables (mean-block)

gamma

posterior variance of W (variance-block, known clusters)

mu

posterior mean of W (variance-block, known clusters)

alpha

cluster proportions (unknown clusters)

M

variational means of W (variance-block, unknown clusters)

S

variational variances of W (variance-block, unknown clusters)

ll_list

list of log-lik (elbo) values

warm_started

whether optim_initialize() should treat the model as already initialized (reuse B/Omega/dm1/C/alpha/M/S as they stand) rather than recomputing a fresh heuristic initialization. Set by $warm_start_from() and by $split()/$merge().

clustering_init

initial clustering

Returns

Update the current object in place

NormalBlockBase$optimize()

calls optimization (EM or heuristic) and updates relevant fields

Usage

NormalBlockBase$optimize(
  control = list(niter = 500, threshold = 1e-04, fixed_point_niter = 5),
  warn = TRUE
)

Arguments

control

a list for controlling the optimization process

warn

whether to warn when the (V)EM stops at the niter cap without reaching threshold (see private$warn_if_not_converged()). Set to FALSE for deliberately-truncated trial fits (cheap candidate scoring in candidates_split()/candidates_merge(), the sparsity-path warm-start probe in NormalBlockCollectionSparsity) where stopping at the cap is expected and not a sign of trouble.

Returns

optimizes the model and updates its parameters

NormalBlockBase$best_of_inits()

Try several clustering-initialization heuristics and keep the best-ELBO converged fit (see NB_control()'s clustering_init for the heuristics and the rationale behind the default). Every candidate is first screened with a short trial_niter run (same idea as candidates_split()/candidates_merge()), and only the max_training best-screened ones are fully retrained with control.

Usage

NormalBlockBase$best_of_inits(
  inits = private$default_inits,
  trial_niter = 10,
  max_training = 2,
  control = list(niter = 500, threshold = 1e-04, fixed_point_niter = 5)
)

Arguments

inits

vector of clustering-heuristic names to try; defaults to the model family's own preferred order (private$default_inits)

trial_niter

number of (V)EM iterations used to cheaply screen every candidate in inits before fully retraining the best few

max_training

how many of the screened candidates (best loglik after trial_niter iterations) get fully retrained with control

control

optimize() control list (niter/threshold) used for the final full retraining of the max_training best candidates

Returns

a new, already-optimized model. Does not mutate the current object; reassign the result (model <- model$best_of_inits()).

NormalBlockBase$warm_start_from()

Seed this model's starting parameters from another, already-optimized model of the same family and q, instead of a fresh heuristic clustering. Used by the sparsity paths to warm-start each penalty from the previous one's solution.

Usage

NormalBlockBase$warm_start_from(other)

Arguments

other

a model of the same class, already optimized

Returns

Update the current object in place with other's parameters

NormalBlockBase$candidates_split()

generate and select a set of candidate models by splitting the clusters of the current model

Usage

NormalBlockBase$candidates_split(trial_niter = 5, split_rule = NULL)

Arguments

trial_niter

number of (V)EM iterations used to cheaply score each candidate before the caller fully re-optimizes the best few – kept short on purpose.

split_rule

passed to split() as its rule: "kmeans", "noise", or NULL for the family's default

NormalBlockBase$candidates_merge()

generate and select a set of candidate models by merging the clusters of the current model

Usage

NormalBlockBase$candidates_merge(max_candidates = 30, trial_niter = 2)

Arguments

max_candidates

merge candidates are, unlike split's, quadratic in q (choose(q, q-2) pairs): beyond max_candidates pairs, only the most promising ones are actually built and trial-optimized, ranked by the family's own private$merge_score(). Set to Inf to always try every pair.

trial_niter

see $candidates_split()

NormalBlockBase$heldout_loglik()

Log-likelihood of new observations at the fitted parameters and, for an unknown clustering, at the MAP partition (see normal_block_cv()). It is exact, computed for variance-block models with q x q matrices only (Woodbury identity), and given on Y's original scale.

Usage

NormalBlockBase$heldout_loglik(newdata, per_observation = FALSE)

Arguments

newdata

a NormalBlockData object with the same variables and covariates (and zero-inflation covariates) as the training data.

per_observation

whether to return one value per observation rather than their sum.

Returns

the held-out log-likelihood, or a vector of newdata$n values

NormalBlockBase$predict()

Predicts the mean of Y for new covariates X, in Y's original units. For the variance-block family, X B: the latent block signals average out, so that on the training X it differs from fitted(), which adds their posterior mean. The mean-block family overrides it.

Usage

NormalBlockBase$predict(new_X)

Arguments

new_X

new set of covariates.

Returns

A n*p prediction matrix for new observations

NormalBlockBase$latent_network()

Extract the network encoded by Omega, as a matrix rather than a plot (see $plot_network()): between clusters for the variance-block family, between variables for the mean-block family.

Usage

NormalBlockBase$latent_network(type = c("partial_cor", "support", "precision"))

Arguments

type

edge value in the network: "support" (binary edges), "precision" (entries of the precision matrix, on the scale of the fit) or "partial_cor" (partial correlations)

Returns

a sparse square matrix, q x q (variance-block) or p x p (mean-block), with named rows and columns

NormalBlockBase$plot_loglik()

plots the evolution of the objective (log-likelihood or ELBO) across the (V)EM iterations of the last call to optimize().

Usage

NormalBlockBase$plot_loglik(show_increment = TRUE)

Arguments

show_increment

whether to add a second panel with the (log10) absolute increment between iterations and the convergence threshold (distinguishes true convergence from a flat-looking objective trace).

Returns

a ggplot2::ggplot graph

NormalBlockBase$plot_network()

Plot the network encoded by Omega (see $latent_network() to extract it as a matrix).

Usage

NormalBlockBase$plot_network(
  type = c("partial_cor", "support"),
  output = c("igraph", "corrplot"),
  edge.color = c("#F8766D", "#00BFC4"),
  remove.isolated = FALSE,
  node.labels = NULL,
  layout = igraph::layout_in_circle,
  plot = TRUE
)

Arguments

type

edge value in the network: "partial_cor" (partial correlations) or "support" (binary edges).

output

Output type. Either igraph (for the network) or corrplot (for the adjacency matrix)

edge.color

Length 2 color vector. Color for positive/negative edges. Default is c("#F8766D", "#00BFC4"). Only relevant for igraph output.

remove.isolated

if TRUE, isolated node are remove before plotting. Only relevant for igraph output.

node.labels

vector of character. The labels of the nodes. By default, the cluster names (variance-block) or the variable names (mean-block), as in $latent_network().

layout

an igraph layout function, applied to the graph without its edge weights, or a matrix of node coordinates. Only relevant for igraph output.

plot

logical. Should the final network be displayed or only sent back to the user. Default is TRUE.
